theory.intro: Some circle problems need more than one property. A diagram can combine a chord property, an angle property and a cyclic quadrilateral property, sometimes side by side and sometimes with the result of one feeding into the next.
facts: Identify every configuration first — equal or perpendicular chords, central or circumference angles, a diameter, a cyclic quadrilateral.
A diameter gives the angle in a semicircle, and, because the centre lies on it, a chord perpendicular to it is bisected.
Equal chords give equal angles at the centre, and so equal angles at the circumference standing on them.
Work one property at a time, using each result as an input to the next.
steps: List every chord, angle and quadrilateral configuration shown in the diagram.
Solve using the first property that can be applied directly from the given information.
Feed that result into the next applicable property.
Repeat until every unknown is found, and check the results are consistent (e.g. angles sum correctly).

foundation.solution_text:
$\angle ACB = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle)
$BC = \sqrt{AB^2 - AC^2} = \sqrt{20^2-12^2} = \sqrt{400-144} = \sqrt{256} = 16$ cm
$DM = 16 \div 2 = 8$ cm (perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord)
$OM = \sqrt{OD^2 - DM^2}$, where $OD = 10$ cm (radius, half of $AB$)
$OM = \sqrt{10^2-8^2} = \sqrt{100-64} = \sqrt{36} = 6$ cm

$\angle AOB = \angle COD$ (equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre)
$\angle AOB = 88^{\circ}$
$\angle AEB = \angle AOB \div 2$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference)
$x = 88^{\circ} \div 2 = 44^{\circ}$

$\angle ABC = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle, since $AC$ is a diameter)
$\angle BCA = 180^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} - 35^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle ABC$)
$x = 55^{\circ}$
$\angle ADC = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle at $D$)
$\angle DCA = 180^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} - 40^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle ADC$)
$y = 50^{\circ}$

$\angle BCD = 180^{\circ} - \angle BAD$ (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary)
$\angle BCD = 180^{\circ} - 104^{\circ} = 76^{\circ}$
$AB = AD$, so equal chords subtend equal angles at the circumference: $\angle BCA = \angle ACD$, and together they make $\angle BCD$
$x = y = 76^{\circ} \div 2 = 38^{\circ}$

$\angle ABC = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle, since $AC$ is a diameter)
$AB = BC$, so $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles, with $\angle BAC = \angle BCA$
$\angle BAC = \angle BCA = (180^{\circ} - 90^{\circ}) \div 2$ (angle sum of $\triangle ABC$)
$= 45^{\circ}$

$\angle ABC = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle)
$AC = \sqrt{AB^2+BC^2} = \sqrt{8^2+6^2} = \sqrt{100} = 10$ cm
$\angle ADC = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle at $D$)
$DC = \sqrt{AC^2-AD^2} = \sqrt{10^2-6^2} = \sqrt{64} = 8$ cm

development.solution_text:
$\angle CBE = \angle ADC$ (exterior angle equals the opposite interior angle)
$\angle ADC = 118^{\circ}$
$\angle ABC = 180^{\circ} - \angle ADC$ (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary)
$\angle ABC = 180^{\circ} - 118^{\circ} = 62^{\circ}$
$AD = DC$, so equal chords subtend equal angles at the circumference: $\angle ABD = \angle DBC$, and together they make $\angle ABC$
$x = y = 62^{\circ} \div 2 = 31^{\circ}$

$\angle BAD = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle)
$BD = \sqrt{AB^2+AD^2} = \sqrt{6^2+8^2} = \sqrt{100} = 10$ cm
$\angle BCD = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle at $C$)
$DC = \sqrt{BD^2-BC^2} = \sqrt{10^2-6^2} = \sqrt{64} = 8$ cm

$\angle ADE = \angle ABC$? — the exterior angle at $D$ equals the interior angle opposite $D$, which is $\angle ABC$.
$\angle ABC = 75^{\circ}$
$\angle AOC = \angle ABC \times 2$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc)
$x = 75^{\circ} \times 2 = 150^{\circ}$

$AB = CD$, so $\angle AOB = \angle COD$ (equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre)
$\angle AOB = \angle AEB \times 2 = 64^{\circ}$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference)
$\angle COD = 64^{\circ}$ too, so $\angle CFD = \angle COD \div 2$
$x = 64^{\circ} \div 2 = 32^{\circ}$

Kai is not correct.
Equal chords $AB$ and $CD$ only guarantee equal arcs (and equal central angles) — they say nothing about the size of the quadrilateral's interior angles.
$ABCD$ can have $AB = CD$ while its angles are not all $90^{\circ}$, so it need not be a rectangle.

$\angle ABC = \angle AOC \div 2$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference)
$\angle ABC = 160^{\circ} \div 2 = 80^{\circ}$
$\angle ADE = \angle ABC$ (exterior angle equals the opposite interior angle)
$x = 80^{\circ}$

mastery.solution_text:
$O$ lies on diameter $AC$, so $OM$ is part of the line $AC$.
Since $BD \perp AC$ at $M$, this means $OM \perp BD$ too.
The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so $M$ is the midpoint of $BD$.
$OM = OA - AM = 10 - 4 = 6$ cm
In right-angled $\triangle OMB$: $OB = 10$ cm (radius), $OM = 6$ cm
$BM = \sqrt{OB^2-OM^2} = \sqrt{100-36} = \sqrt{64} = 8$ cm
$BD = 2 \times BM = 16$ cm

$\angle DCE = \angle DAB$ (exterior angle equals the opposite interior angle)
$\angle DAB = 132^{\circ}$
$AB = AD$, so $\triangle ABD$ is isosceles, with $\angle ABD = \angle ADB$
$\angle ABD = \angle ADB = (180^{\circ}-132^{\circ}) \div 2$ (angle sum of $\triangle ABD$)
$= 24^{\circ}$

$AB = BC$ (given)
$\angle AOB = \angle BOC$ (equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre)
$\angle ADB = \angle AOB \div 2$ and $\angle BDC = \angle BOC \div 2$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc)
$\therefore \angle ADB = \angle BDC$
$\angle ADC = \angle ADB + \angle BDC$, and these two parts are equal, so $BD$ bisects $\angle ADC$.
